title: Optimize walkthrough - quantization profiles (INT8/FP8) quality vs latency
summary: Redwood team walked Atlas Health through Optimize's quantization profile tooling. Discussed INT8 and FP8 profiles, expected latency improvements, and potential quality regressions. Covered calibration procedures, test plans for a pilot, and next steps to run a 1k prompt benchmark. Atlas raised concerns about hallucinations and auditability; Redwood proposed fallback to FP16 and per-route quality thresholds.
next_steps: Redwood to share sample quantization profile and calibration guide
Atlas to provide 200 representative prompts and metrics baseline by 2026-03-28
Schedule pilot benchmark run week of 2026-04-06
SE to run quick latency/quality comparison on Atlas sample and share spreadsheet
action_items: Leah Carter: Send quantization profile templates + calibration doc by 2026-03-23
Miguel Santos: Prepare benchmark script and spreadsheet, run internal sanity tests by 2026-03-25
Samir Patel: Export 200 prompts and baseline outputs (redacted) by 2026-03-28
transcript:
[00:00] Leah Carter: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining uh today it's an Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles INT8 and FP8 and quality vs latency tradeoffs. I'm Leah from Redwood, joined by Miguel on the SE side and Priya who runs post-sales.
[00:17] Ellen Zhao: Hi thanks, we've been excited to see how much cost we can save without hurting inference quality, especially in clinical summarization.
[00:25] Miguel Santos: Yeah totally, we'll try to keep it pragmatic. Quick agenda: show Optimize UI for quant profiles, run a small live comparison (latency and quality metrics), then talk about calibration and rollback.
[00:40] Ravi Menon: Quick note from infra - our stack is GKE, we use TF serving for other stuff, and we're evaluating Dedicated vs hosted. Data residency requirement for EU patients.
[00:51] Leah Carter: Noted - we'll call out Dedicated and Private options and KMS integration.
[00:56] [01:20] Miguel Santos: Pulling up the Optimize console now, you can see here the quantization profiles tab - we have prebuilt profiles for INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric, and FP8. The UI shows an expected latency delta and an accuracy delta per profile against your baseline (typically FP16).
[01:40] Samir Patel: How accurate are those numbers? I mean is that from public benchmarks or Redwood's internal runs?
[01:46] Miguel Santos: Good question. They are derived from our catalog runs on reference prompts and also from per-model distillation runs. For customer's data, we recommend running a benchmark using your prompt set because distribution matters.
[01:58] [02:10] Maya Lopez: Do you support layerwise quant or is it whole-model only?
[02:15] Miguel Santos: We support per-layer profiles - Optimize can create a "hybrid profile" that keeps sensitive layers in FP16 and quantizes others to INT8 or FP8. That's often where most of the quality is preserved while getting latency benefits.
[02:30] Ellen Zhao: Can you explain the difference between INT8 and FP8 in practice? We're seeing FP8 pop up a lot but worried about determinism.
[02:38] Miguel Santos: Sure — INT8 is integer quant which gives good throughput on a wide range of kernels and is very deterministic. FP8 is an 8-bit floating representation that often preserves small-value dynamics better, so it can give higher quality for some transformer layers while still being faster than FP16. FP8 rollout maturity depends on the runtime and hardware support; we test on our supported HW matrix and mark profiles as "Verified" when passing our regressions.
[03:10] [03:40] Samir Patel: Any rules of thumb for expected latency improvement?"
[03:45] Miguel Santos: Typical numbers we've seen: INT8 can give 1.6-2.5x throughput improvement (so latency down ~40-60% in steady-state for token generation) depending on sequence length and batching. FP8 often sits between FP16 and INT8 — maybe 1.3-1.8x. Those ranges vary a lot with kernel support and KV cache behavior.
[04:10] Maya Lopez: What about hallucination/regression? We can't have increased hallucinations in clinical outputs.
[04:16] Miguel Santos: Important point. We run quality checks: accuracy metrics (ROUGE/BLEU where applicable), hallucination heuristics, and domain-specific checks. Optimize will produce a delta report and highlight prompts with largest divergences so you can spot regressions quickly. We also recommend canarying a profile on a subset of traffic with automatic fallback to FP16 if quality thresholds breach.
[04:45] [05:20] Ellen Zhao: So is the fallback dynamic per request or per route? We need per-route control in our API gateway.
[05:25] Leah Carter: You can set policies per-route in Redwood Console; Optimize suggests a profile and you can attach rollout rules — canary 5% then 25 etc, or failover immediately on metrics. That ties into tracing so you can see token-level latencies and errors.
[05:48] Samir Patel: Can you show the actual comparison UI for a model?
[05:53] Miguel Santos: Yep, loading sample model -> here's a baseline FP16 run on 10 prompts, latencies in ms per prompt, here's INT8 profile run, and FP8 run. You'll see in this sample the INT8 reduces median latency from 210ms to 95ms for 128-token contexts; FP8 reduces to 130ms with slightly better quality than INT8.
[06:20] [06:45] Miguel Santos: (typing) note: the sample model here is a 7B-ish open model; larger models have different breakpoints where FP8 can be more beneficial.
[06:58] Ellen Zhao: Those numbers help. Can you export the raw results? We want CSV.
[07:03] Miguel Santos: Yes export CSV and we also create a per-prompt diff sheet that flags semantic drift.
[07:12] [07:40] Priya Kapoor: On post-sales side, we'll help run a structured bench: you share prompts, we run FP16 baseline, then INT8 and FP8 profiles, then share a report with suggested hybrid profile.
[07:55] Ravi Menon: What about quantization calibration? Is there any on-device calibration step that touches customer data?
[08:02] Miguel Santos: Calibration uses representative inputs — we can run calibration in your private environment if necessary. The calibration artifacts are numeric summaries (scales/zeros) not raw prompts; however if you require, we can run in your VPC or on-prem and deliver only the profile.
[08:23] [08:40] Samir Patel: Security question - audit logs and crypto? We need KMS and HSM support for keys and SOC2 details.
[08:47] Leah Carter: Redwood supports external KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments; we have SOC 2 Type II and can provide audit artifacts as part of enterprise security pack. We'll send the security brief.
[09:05] [09:30] Miguel Santos: Back to quality - here's an example where INT8 introduces a minor truncation on numeric outputs; Optimize tags that prompt and shows diffs. You can create an acceptability rule that forces FP16 on routes that touch those prompts or that have hallucination scores above threshold.
[09:55] Maya Lopez: That acceptability rule — is it configurable per API key?
[10:00] Leah Carter: Yes per-route and per-api-key policies are supported.
[10:05] [10:30] Samir Patel: Can we test with our 200 clinical prompts?
[10:35] Miguel Santos: Absolutely, that would be ideal. For the pilot we usually ask for 200-1k prompts depending on variability. We'll run baseline vs INT8 vs FP8, produce latency percentiles, and quality deltas including a small human-reviewed sample.
[10:55] [11:20] Ellen Zhao: How long does a full 1k prompt benchmark take?
[11:25] Miguel Santos: End-to-end, including human review, typically 3-5 days. Automated runs are a few hours depending on model size and concurrency.
[11:38] [12:00] Miguel Santos: Also worth noting caching: if your traffic benefits from prefix caching the latency delta improves because repeated prefix keys avoid recompute. We saw some clients get 30% extra gains when cache-hit rates are high.
[12:22] Samir Patel: Any limitations around batch size? We have bursts and prefer low tail latency.
[12:28] Miguel Santos: The runtime supports adaptive batching; Optimize recommends batch sizes under your latency SLO. INT8 tends to favor larger batches for throughput but we can configure micro-batching to maintain tail latencies.
[12:50] [13:20] Leah Carter: Quick demo note - the console will also show cost per token estimate after profile change. That helps you measure dollars/token vs quality tradeoffs.
[13:35] Maya Lopez: Do you support quant-aware training or finetuning to recover quality?
[13:40] Miguel Santos: We don't provide QAT end-to-end as a managed service today but we do have guidance. Some customers run a small fine-tune pass and then quantize which helps. Optimize supports uploading a finetuned artifact and will profile it.
[14:05] [14:40] Ellen Zhao: Ok let's talk rollback - if a profile causes regression, timeline to roll back?
[14:45] Miguel Santos: Rolling back is immediate at routing layer — you can flip back to FP16 or switch to a hybrid profile. We keep profile versioning and you can schedule automatic rollback triggers when metrics breach thresholds.
[15:05] [15:30] Priya Kapoor: We'll also help set the alerting: on quality delta or error rate.
[15:40] Samir Patel: Are there any models you wouldn't recommend quantizing?
[15:45] Miguel Santos: Edge cases: very small models (<1B) sometimes don't benefit; some heavily finetuned safety-critical models where distribution shift is tiny also warrant caution. That's why we always benchmark.
[16:05] [16:40] Maya Lopez: Any hardware recommendations? We're multi-cloud.
[16:45] Miguel Santos: FP8 benefits on A100-class and newer Ampere/Blackwell kernels with FP8 support; INT8 runs broadly on most GPUs but will be faster on optimized tensor cores. We'll include a hardware compatibility matrix in the doc pack.
[17:10] [17:40] Ellen Zhao: For our POC, we want minimal changes to infra. Can you run the benchmark against a hosted Redwood instance but with data masked?
[17:47] Leah Carter: Yes we can host a test env; alternatively run entirely in your VPC. For masking, we recommend redaction scripts pre-run. We'll provide guidance.
[18:05] [18:30] Miguel Santos: Showing the per-prompt diff report now - you can click into each prompt and see token-level attention to where outputs diverge. It also surfaces hallucination heuristics.
[18:55] Samir Patel: Nice. I see some spikes in tail latency for INT8 on one prompt - looks like KV cache miss pattern?
[19:01] Miguel Santos: Yep that's typically KV cache pressure. For some workloads we recommend hybrid -- keep KV heavy layers in FP16 to avoid tail regressions.
[19:20] [19:50] Ellen Zhao: Pricing impact? ballpark savings?
[19:55] Leah Carter: Typical cost reduction per-token can be 20-60% depending on profile and caching. We'll put numbers on the POC spreadsheet.
[20:12] [20:40] Samir Patel: What's the next step to start?
[20:45] Leah Carter: If you can send 200 representative prompts and a baseline output export, Miguel and team will run a benchmark and return a report with recommended profile and rollout plan. We'll also send security docs and the quantization calibration guide.
[21:05] [21:30] Maya Lopez: Timeline for the report?
[21:35] Miguel Santos: Automated runs same day, full report with human review within 3 business days.
[21:50] [22:15] Ellen Zhao: Any final gotchas?
[22:20] Miguel Santos: Watch out for distribution mismatch: if prompts later change, quality deltas can shift - we recommend scheduled re-profiling every quarter or on major model changes. Also beware of mixed-precision on multi-GPU setups, we provide config templates.
[22:45] [23:10] Leah Carter: Recap: Redwood to send quant profiles + calibration doc + security brief; Atlas to send 200 prompts and baseline outputs; SE to run benchmark and share spreadsheet; schedule pilot week of 4/6.
[23:35] Samir Patel: Sounds good, we'll aim for 3/28 with prompts.
[23:40] Ellen Zhao: Thank you all.
[23:45] Miguel Santos: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[23:50] Priya Kapoor: End call.
